title: Verdure alla Griglia
subtitle: Italian chargrilled vegetables with olive oil and herbs
excerpt: Verdure alla griglia is the Italian method for chargrilled vegetables: courgettes, aubergines, peppers, and red onions charred on a griddle pan or grill, then dressed while still warm with good olive oil, garlic, and fresh herbs. The charring is the point: pale, gently steamed vegetables are not the same dish.
sourceNotes: Verdure alla griglia is a staple of Italian antipasto and summer eating. Chargrilling vegetables over embers or on a ridged griddle is documented throughout Italian regional cooking, particularly in southern Italy, where vegetables are eaten as a main course as often as a side dish.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale in direct proportion. Works well made in large quantities for a spread.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Grilled vegetables are better after resting for 30 minutes to 2 hours at room temperature as the dressing soaks in. Can be made up to 6 hours ahead.

content.text: Verdure alla griglia depends on the char. Each vegetable needs direct, very high heat to develop the dark, caramelised grill marks and smoky depth that makes the difference between grilled vegetables and boiled ones with lines on them. Get the griddle pan very hot before anything goes on it, and do not move the vegetables once they are on the grill: let them sit until the char lines form.

items.prepNote: cut into 1 cm wedges through the root

content.text: Heat a ridged griddle pan over high heat until very hot: a drop of water should evaporate immediately on contact. Brush lightly with a little olive oil.

Grill the vegetables in batches, not overlapping. Place them on the griddle and do not move them for 3 to 4 minutes until char marks form. Turn and grill the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. Each vegetable type cooks at its own pace: courgettes 6 minutes total, aubergines 8 to 10 minutes, peppers 8 minutes, onions 8 to 10 minutes.
As each batch comes off the griddle, layer into a wide serving dish. Season with salt as you go.

Mix the olive oil, garlic, basil, parsley, and lemon juice if using. Pour over the warm grilled vegetables. Turn gently so the dressing coats everything. Leave to rest at room temperature for at least 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Vegetables are steamed and pale rather than charred
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough, or too many vegetables were added at once
items.fix: Grill in small batches and preheat the pan thoroughly. Crowding drops the temperature and causes steaming.

items.symptom: Aubergine is undercooked and spongy inside
items.cause: Slices were too thick or cooking time was too short
items.fix: Aubergine needs at least 4 to 5 minutes per side on a hot griddle to cook through. Press gently with a spatula: it should give easily when done.

items.symptom: Onion wedges autumn apart on the griddle
items.cause: Cut through the root rather than leaving it intact
items.fix: Always cut onion wedges from root to tip, keeping a little root at the base to hold the layers together.

content.text: Verdure alla griglia appears at the start of most Italian summer meals as an antipasto. It sits alongside bruschetta and sliced meats. In southern Italian cooking it is also eaten as a main course. A platter of grilled vegetables with good bread is a filling meal. The technique of grilling over high heat and dressing while warm with olive oil and herbs is used throughout Italy.
